title: Neon Vault
premise: A neon sci-fi relic scanner game where the player spends vault funds to reveal randomized relic cards and chase valuable rare finds before going broke.
interaction_model: Single-screen tap/click interactions with a primary scan button, menu navigation, and an archive screen for collection progress.
objective: Spend funds to scan relics, win payouts from better rarities, and unlock all relic tiers in the archive before hitting lockout.
progression: Short-run economy progression through repeated paid scans, random rarity reveals, balance swings from payouts, and persistent archive completion across sessions.
theme: Cyberpunk neon vault, futuristic relic recovery, scanner interface, techno-arcane treasure hunting.
mood: Glossy, suspenseful, arcade-like, rewarding, slightly casino-coded but stylized as sci-fi treasure discovery.
likely_audience: Players who enjoy casual gacha reveals, collectible progression, flashy UI feedback, and short mobile-friendly arcade sessions.
confidence_notes: High confidence that the core loop is a tap-to-reveal gacha or loot-draw game with a simple bankroll mechanic.
High confidence that archive completion is an intended secondary progression layer.
Moderate confidence that the design aims to feel like a lightweight risk-reward slot analogue rather than a pure idle clicker.
recreation_prompt: Create a mobile-friendly single-screen neon sci-fi relic draw game called Neon Vault where the player starts with a fixed pool of money, pays a fee each time they tap a large SCAN button, and watches a futuristic card shake and flip to reveal one of five weighted-random relic rarities ranging from a worthless common scrap outcome to a jackpot legendary artifact. Present the game as a stylish cyber vault interface with a start screen, gameplay screen, archive screen, and lockout game-over overlay. Use a glossy purple-cyan-pink visual palette, animated background grid, glowing glass panels, dramatic card flip animation, procedural-looking relic art, rarity glows, celebratory particles, and punchy sound feedback. The core loop should be: spend money, reveal a relic, apply a payout multiplier based on rarity, update the balance, unlock that relic tier in a persistent archive, and continue scanning until the player runs out of funds. Include collection progression by showing all five relic slots in an archive with locked placeholders until discovered. Make rare, epic, and legendary reveals feel especially exciting with stronger audiovisual effects and reaction media, while bad rolls should feel disappointing and eventually trigger a lockout state with a restart option that restores starting funds. Keep controls simple and tap-first, make the UI readable on phones, and emphasize anticipation, reveal spectacle, bankroll tension, and completion of the relic archive.
